newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold re-exports limited by weaker rupee.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold re-exports limited by weaker rupee.

text.p: A weaker rupee has capped Indian demand for gold from the Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai despite lower bullion prices and the prospect of wedding and festival-related gold demand, Dubai traders said on Sunday.

Though demand into India and Pakistan remains upbeat after the end of monsoon rains, subcontinent importers face higher costs because of the depreciation of the Indian rupee against the dollar and a narrow trading arbitrage from Dubai to Bombay.

"The bearish trend in the international market will not be of much help to the Indian gold and silver demand as the Indian rupee is trending lower," said Sultan Satani at Dubai-based Satco Global Trading.
The rupee was last quoted at 35.65 to the dollar, down from 35.45 on September 1 close.
"It will continue to keep prices on the high side," one trader said.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar (TT) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted at 5,321 UAE dirhams ($1,449.86), down 22 dirhams on the week. Bombay TTs were quoted at $1,693.25.
Spot bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $385.00-$385.40 per ounce, losing $1.55 in an eight-day slide.
Dubai is the main feeder market into India which is the world's single largest gold consumer.
Indian subcontinent import demand is expected to take off as early as the middle of this month ahead of India's traditional wedding and festival season which is in full flow by October.
"Trading is sure to take off very soon," one trader involved in the Dubai-Bombay route said.
Silver was quoted at $166 a kilo in Dubai and $204 a kilo in Bombay.
